name: Connecticut Data Privacy Act

control_flags.objectives: The numbered items a subsection lists inline, only where every one must be met.

scoring.summary: Percentage of applicable requirements that are implemented. The Act defines no score; this percentage is an HCG measure of progress.

rules.summary: A requirement is met only when every element it lists is met.

Part I applies to businesses that controlled or processed personal data of at least 100,000 consumers in the preceding year, or of at least 25,000 consumers while deriving over 25% of gross revenue from selling personal data.

rules.summary: A consumer rights request is answered without undue delay and within 45 days of receipt; the period may be extended once by 45 days.

rules.summary: An appeal of a refused request is decided and answered in writing within 60 days of receipt.

glossary.definition: The Connecticut Data Privacy Act, Connecticut's comprehensive consumer privacy law, in force since 1 July 2023.
The person that, alone or jointly with others, determines the purpose and means of processing personal data.
A person that processes personal data on behalf of a controller.
Personal data a controller uses to identify a consumer's physical or mental health condition or diagnosis, including gender-affirming and reproductive or sexual health data.

glossary.term: Heightened risk of harm to minors
glossary.definition: Processing of a minor's personal data in a way that presents a reasonably foreseeable risk of unfair treatment, financial or physical injury, or intrusion on the minor's privacy; Part II requires assessments and safeguards for it.
